problem: Prior two-stage (search then pathfind) object navigation methods only add parallel network modules but train with a single sparse or shortest-path reward that ignores the different goals of the two stages, so they under-train or overfit training scenes. Generic visual encoders also lack depth/spatial perception.
motivation: Humans explore before seeing the target, then head straight to it, with different motivations at each phase. Single-stage rewards ignore this causal structure, and encoders pretrained on classification or RGB-only MAE cannot tell explored from unexplored areas or judge distance to the target from monocular RGB.
key_idea: Split each episode into a searching stage (area-coverage exploration reward) and a pathfinding stage (distance reward including rotations) at the first confident detection of the target, and pretrain the ViT encoder with an RGB-masked autoencoder that also reconstructs depth (DE-MAE).
insight: The two components are complementary: in the AI2-THOR ablation, the exploration reward mainly improves SSR and SSSPL, the distance reward mainly improves NSNPL, and combining them beats either alone. DE-MAE alone gives only modest gains, but combined with TSRM it gives the best results (SR 86.73 vs 85.70 without it), so better perception pays off only when the reward shapes strategy. Random-crop augmentation in pretraining removes the DE-MAE benefit (SPL 48.36 with crop vs 49.35 without), because cropping breaks the image-to-real-space mapping under fixed camera intrinsics.
method: Two-Stage Reward Mechanism (TSRM): each episode starts in the searching stage and switches irreversibly to pathfinding when DETR confidence for the target first exceeds C_target=0.7.

Searching-stage exploration reward: K_e × area of newly observed region, where the observed region is the union of isosceles trapezoids per position, clipped to the room footprint from the AI2-THOR API.

Pathfinding-stage distance reward: K_d × reduction in graph distance to any successful terminal state on a directed grid graph whose edges are MoveAhead/Rotate actions with unit weight, so rotations are rewarded or penalized. Distances are precomputed by multi-source shortest path.

DE-MAE pretraining: ViT-Base encoder on masked RGB, small ViT decoder with two linear heads reconstructing RGB (masked patches) and depth (all patches) with MSE. Pretrained on ~2M RGB-D AI2-THOR images with horizontal flip only.

Policy network: DE-MAE ViT features plus a conv layer, IOM's NTWA target-memory embedding of DETR features, and a previous-action embedding are concatenated into the state and fed to an LSTM policy trained with A3C.
Other rewards: collision penalty -0.1 on repeated collision, slack penalty -0.01 per step, +5 on success.
SSSPL metric: Nav_i × L*_search / max(L_search, L*_search), measuring search efficiency against the shortest path to any position satisfying the dividing-point criterion.

setting.backbone: ViT-Base pretrained with DE-MAE + IOM NTWA target aggregator + LSTM policy (A3C); DETR for target detection
setting.training_data: DE-MAE pretraining on ~2M RGB-D images from AI2-THOR training scenes; RL for 1.5M episodes on AI2-THOR/RoboTHOR training scenes
setting.observation: monocular egocentric RGB (depth used only in pretraining) plus DETR target detection features
setting.action_space: discrete low-level: MoveAhead, RotateLeft, RotateRight, LookDown, LookUp, Done
setting.privileged: none at test time (room bounds, grid graph and distances are used only for training rewards)

numbers.extra: max episode length 100; success within 1 m

numbers.eval_set_note: targets with optimal trajectory length L>=5

numbers.evidence: Table 2 ablation, all three components checked

numbers_note: AI2-THOR split is not explicitly labeled in the results table (rooms: 20 train / 5 val / 5 test per type), so 'test' is assumed. The paper's own results are reported only on AI2-THOR and RoboTHOR, which are not canonical benchmark names except RoboTHOR.
results: On AI2-THOR/RoboTHOR the method reaches SR 86.73/74.93 and SPL 50.48/40.37, beating the previous best MT (85.47/73.86 SR, 47.02/38.46 SPL) and IOM. Gains are largest in SPL on AI2-THOR (+3.46) and hold on the L>=5 subset (SR 81.71 vs 80.08).
limitations: Evaluated only on AI2-THOR and RoboTHOR in simulation, with no real-robot experiments.
Relies on room footprint, grid graph, and precomputed distances from simulator APIs for reward computation, and on a hand-tuned DETR confidence threshold (0.7) as stage boundary.
DE-MAE requires in-domain RGB-D pretraining data from the simulator scenes and is sensitive to augmentation; gains from the encoder alone are small.
